steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Film movements are coherent groups of filmmakers who share aesthetic principles, production methods and ideological commitments during a specific historical period. | Key Fact: Italian Neo-Realism emerged after World War II, rejecting studio artificiality in favour of location shooting, non-professional actors and stories about working-class struggle. | Key Fact: The French New Wave of the late 1950s and 1960s challenged mainstream French cinema with location filming, handheld camera, jump cuts and self-reflexive storytelling. | Key Fact: German Expressionism of the 1920s used distorted set design, exaggerated shadows and stylised performance to convey psychological turmoil and social anxiety in post-World War I Germany.
